title: Warp-STAR: High-Performance, Differentiable GPU-Accelerated Static Timing Analysis Through Warp-Oriented Parallel Orchestration
evidence_span: Static timing analysis is a bottleneck; Warp-STAR removes intra-warp load imbalance through warp-level orchestration, reports 2.4X speedup over prior GPU STA and 1.7X in timing-driven global placement, and supports differentiable gradient analysis.
problem: GPU static timing analysis suffers from intra-warp load imbalance on irregular circuit graphs, limiting timing-analysis and placement-flow throughput.
method_or_artifact: Warp-level parallel orchestration for a differentiable GPU-accelerated static timing analysis engine.
workload_or_benchmark: Static timing analysis on irregular circuit graphs; integration into timing-driven global placement; differentiable gradient analysis.
metrics: minimal overhead for differentiable gradient analysis
limits: The public description does not expose full circuit suites, absolute runtime, quality tradeoffs, or transfer limits.

title: Moduplace: LLM-Assisted Modular PCB Placement via Preference-Optimized Constraint Graph Generation
evidence_span: ModuPlace partitions component sets into modules at different granularities, uses LLM fine-tuning and preference optimization for constraint-graph generation, and reports superior placement quality across all metrics versus baselines.
problem: Existing automated PCB placement systems do not express user preferences well and lack modular placement, producing impractical or poor-quality layouts.
method_or_artifact: LLM-assisted hierarchical modular placement with preference-optimized constraint-graph generation.
workload_or_benchmark: PCB component placement with user requirements and modular component partitions.
metrics: placement quality across all reported metrics
limits: The description does not provide metric names, numerical gains, board-suite composition, or evidence about generalization beyond the evaluated placement tasks.

title: Powerpath: Internal-Probe-Free Search Interval Reduction for Efficient Statistical Sequential Constraint Characterization
evidence_span: Power-path uses a physics-grounded supply-current signature from a mandatory reference-delay simulation, affine lookup-table calibration, and online ridge regression; on post-layout TSMC 5 nm and 12 nm libraries across five PVT corners it reports 1.5X and 3.6X speedups while maintaining signoff-grade accuracy.
problem: Sequential-constraint characterization consumes substantial signoff runtime and traditional path-based approaches fail for toggle-unexpected arcs or require extra SPICE simulations.
method_or_artifact: Internal-probe-free supply-current estimation with affine calibration and online ridge-regression interval tightening.
workload_or_benchmark: Post-layout TSMC 5 nm and 12 nm libraries across five process-voltage-temperature corners; sequential constraint characterization.
metrics: up to 80% of signoff runtime addressed
limits: The description does not expose absolute runtime, error distributions, or whether the reported libraries represent broader process technologies.

title: Quantum Circuit Synthesis Using an Exact T Library
evidence_span: The work formulates exact T synthesis, canonicalizes Boolean functions under Clifford equivalence, precomputes T-optimal implementations up to seven variables, and reports up to 16% T-count reduction on EPFL benchmarks plus improvements for cryptographic modules.
problem: AND-count minimization is an imperfect proxy for T cost in fault-tolerant quantum synthesis because it misses phase cancellation.
method_or_artifact: Exact T-synthesis formulation with Clifford-equivalence canonicalization, precomputed small-function libraries, and a specialized mapper.
workload_or_benchmark: EPFL benchmarks and cryptographic circuit modules in fault-tolerant quantum synthesis.
metrics: improved best-known T counts for selected cryptographic modules
limits: The public description does not enumerate all circuits, runtime costs, or the scalability boundary of exact precomputation.

title: TDH-GNN: An Efficient Topology-Driven Accelerator for Dynamic Heterogeneous GNN
evidence_span: TDH-GNN uses hyperedge-centric incremental execution to reduce redundant metapath matching; implemented on a Xilinx U280, it reports average speedups of 4.3X and 2.8X and energy savings of 5.9X and 3.7X over leading HGNN accelerators.
problem: Dynamic heterogeneous GNN inference repeats metapath matching and computation as graph structure and semantics evolve.
method_or_artifact: Topology-driven accelerator using hyperedge-centric incremental execution for dynamic metapath updates.
workload_or_benchmark: Dynamic heterogeneous graph neural-network inference with evolving metapath structure; Xilinx U280 implementation.
limits: The description does not identify which workloads correspond to each pair of speedup/energy figures or provide FPGA resource and accuracy tradeoffs.

title: Strix: Re-Thinking NPU Reliability from a System Perspective
evidence_span: Strix spans NPU microarchitecture, ISA, and programming on an open-source SoC, partitions safeguards along the inference pipeline, and reports sub-microsecond fault localization/detection/correction with 1.04X slowdown and minimal hardware overhead.
problem: Monolithic NPU replication creates prohibitive overhead while failing to provide deployable reliability for increasingly fault-prone accelerators.
method_or_artifact: Full-stack reliability framework with pipeline-level fault-mode analysis and targeted safeguards across microarchitecture, ISA, and programming.
workload_or_benchmark: DNN and LLM inference on an open-source SoC NPU, including safety-oriented fault scenarios.
metrics: sub-microsecond fault localization, detection, and correction
limits: The description does not specify fault model coverage, workload set, reliability guarantee, or exact hardware overhead.

title: GEMIR: Graph-Based Joint Modeling of Electromigration and IR Drop for Power Grid
evidence_span: GEMIR jointly predicts node-level static IR drop and edge-level electromigration stress using cross-layer attention, physics-informed constraints for KCL and the Korhonen PDE, and conflict-gated multitask optimization; it reports 40.79% lower IR-drop MAE and 19.35% lower EM-stress RMSE.
problem: Separate EM and IR-drop analysis misses their shared physical structure, while numerical methods are expensive on large designs.
method_or_artifact: Graph-based multitask learning with node-edge attention, physics-informed constraints, and conflict-gated gradient fusion.
workload_or_benchmark: Power-grid analysis for node-level static IR drop and edge-level electromigration-induced stress.
limits: The description does not disclose design sizes, absolute runtime, or the distribution of gains across technologies and workloads.

title: Brain-Like Hyper-Dimensional Graph Learning System with Hardware-Efficient Adaptive Sparsity
evidence_span: HDGAS co-optimizes a lightweight runtime feature filter with a hyper-dimensional graph-learning model, then pairs dynamic sparsification with SpMM hardware; it reports 6.76X/69.31X speedup and 7.58X/80.12X energy-efficiency improvement over GNN accelerators/GPU.
problem: General-purpose CPUs and GPUs handle hyper-dimensional graph learning inefficiently, and not all graph node features contribute equally.
method_or_artifact: Algorithm-hardware co-designed HDGAS accelerator with runtime adaptive feature sparsity and specialized SpMM architecture.
workload_or_benchmark: Hyper-dimensional graph learning workloads with graph node-feature sparsification.
limits: The description does not identify benchmark names, accuracy impact, hardware platform details, or which comparison produces each metric pair.

title: A Differentiable Approach to Task Graph Partitioning: A Case Study in RTL Simulation
evidence_span: DiffPart learns task-graph partitions under real threading conditions and, applied to RTL simulation, reports up to 1.22–55.25X faster runtime across diverse designs than Verilator's partitioning.
problem: General-purpose task-graph partitioning heuristics overlook real threading costs and produce suboptimal RTL-simulation schedules.
method_or_artifact: Differentiable task-graph partitioning framework that learns partitions under operating conditions.
workload_or_benchmark: RTL simulation of diverse designs with dependent task graphs.
limits: The description does not specify design sizes, thread counts, quality constraints, or how the wide speedup range is distributed.

title: BLADE: Bi-Level Bayesian Optimization for Metal-Density-Constrained Multi-Layer Package Power/ground Plane Synthesis
evidence_span: BLADE expands power/ground planes from skeletons under metal-density and degassing constraints, uses a fast IR-drop evaluator with bi-level Bayesian optimization, and evaluates six SiP cases.
problem: Package power/ground planes must maintain power integrity while meeting uniform metal-density constraints that prevent warpage and accommodate degassing holes.
method_or_artifact: Metal-density-aware P/G-plane synthesis with a fast IR-drop evaluator and bi-level Bayesian optimization.
workload_or_benchmark: Six system-in-package power/ground-plane cases with metal-density and degassing constraints.
limits: The description does not expose numerical IR-drop gains, baseline names, or package geometry/process assumptions.

title: Beyond Flat Netlist: Hierarchical Graph Representation Learning for Scalable Analysis of Sequential Circuits
evidence_span: DeepSeq3 uses a two-level circuit representation, dual GNNs, and state-centric reachability pretraining; on large-scale benchmarks it reduces bounded-model-checking solving time by 18% while guaranteeing correctness.
problem: Flat circuit representations do not scale to industrial netlists and fail to represent register-level temporal dynamics for sequential-circuit analysis.
method_or_artifact: Hierarchical combinational-subgraph and register-transfer super-node representation with dual GNNs and state-centric reachability pretraining.
workload_or_benchmark: Large-scale sequential-circuit benchmarks and bounded model checking.

title: Dataflowgen: An MLIR-Based Compiler for Efficient Dataflow Accelerator Generation
evidence_span: DataFlowGen is an open-source MLIR framework with two-level IRs, automated kernel outlining, and dataflow transformations into a hardware-oriented control dataflow graph; experiments report performance improvement with significant resource reduction versus state-of-the-art HLS tools.
problem: Existing HLS tools have difficulty mapping data-dependent applications into custom hardware because algorithm and microarchitecture concerns appear at mismatched IR levels.
method_or_artifact: Open-source MLIR compiler with two-level intermediate representation, kernel outlining, dataflow transformation, and automated optimization.
workload_or_benchmark: High-level-synthesis kernels and dataflow accelerator generation.
limits: The description does not state numerical gains, benchmark identities, target devices, or compilation-time cost.

title: Gearls: Generalizable Reinforcement Learning Framework for Logic Optimization via Policy Similarity Metric
evidence_span: Gearls uses logic-cone extraction, cut weighting, and a policy-similarity metric for zero-shot RL transfer; on unseen benchmark circuits it reports 31.7% lower WNS, 32.5% lower TNS, and 13% of prior runtime.
problem: Circuit-specific reinforcement-learning optimization requires retraining and has weak generalization to unseen circuits.
method_or_artifact: Logic-cone-aware RL framework with cut-weighted timing representation and policy similarity metric for zero-shot transfer.
workload_or_benchmark: Unseen benchmark circuits in digital logic optimization.
limits: The description does not identify circuit suites, PPA tradeoffs, or whether zero-shot performance holds across technology libraries.

title: GenDSE: Generative CPU Design Space Exploration via Sequential Decision Making
evidence_span: GenDSE reformulates CPU design-space exploration as a sequential decision process, uses a GFlowNet configuration generator and Progressive Sketching, and reduces simulation costs by 90% on average while maintaining superior solution quality.
problem: Surrogate-guided CPU design-space exploration suffers from credit-assignment problems and high simulation sample complexity.
method_or_artifact: Markov decision process with GFlowNet-based configuration generation and Progressive Sketching for data efficiency.
workload_or_benchmark: CPU microarchitecture design-space exploration and simulation.

title: Icarus's Wings: Disabling MoE Offloading Acceleration via a Universal Hidden Prefix Attack

method_or_artifact: Gradient-based universal hidden-prefix attack combining temporal-locality minimization, expert-prefetch misleading, and a target-balancing scheduler.

evidence_span: CANNON implements a CXL near-memory-processing architecture on real hardware, uses a deeply pipelined ANN dataflow with asynchronous hashing and speculative execution, and reports up to two orders of magnitude improvement over CPU and GPU baselines on large-scale vector datasets.

method_or_artifact: CXL-based near-memory processing with fully offloaded pipelined ANN search, asynchronous hashing, and speculative execution.

title: HYPER-CIM: Hierarchical Predictive Exploration and Realizable Design Flow for High-Efficient Digital CIM
evidence_span: HYPER-CIM uses over 8k silicon-consistent points to train a hierarchical PPA surrogate over 297M configurations, fabricates and verifies 28 nm CIM macros, and reports 90.8 TOPS/W, 1.23 TOPS/mm², and cross-level energy/area improvements.
problem: CIM exploration often optimizes only one level and lacks circuit-faithful visibility across macro, accelerator, and architecture decisions.
method_or_artifact: Hierarchical predictive exploration flow with a digital 28 nm CIM template, multi-head circuit-optimization surrogate, Pareto search, and silicon verification.
workload_or_benchmark: Digital compute-in-memory macro and architecture design across tunable precision, storage, channels, pipeline depth, and accumulation length.
